source: docs/architecture-pattern-taxonomy.md (Software Architecture Pattern Taxonomy v1, 2026-11-24); antipattern ids assigned here

concerns.name: System composition and topology
concerns.decision: How is the overall system divided, connected, and executed?

concerns.name: Application organization and domain boundaries
concerns.decision: How are code, business meaning, and dependencies organized inside applications?

concerns.name: Presentation and client architecture
concerns.decision: How are user interaction, rendering, and client state structured?

concerns.name: APIs and service interaction
concerns.decision: How do clients and services invoke, discover, and compose capabilities?

concerns.name: Messaging and event integration
concerns.decision: How do systems exchange, route, transform, and reliably process messages?

concerns.name: Workflow, decisions, and business coordination
concerns.decision: How is multi-step work planned, persisted, completed, and compensated?

concerns.name: Persistence and data ownership
concerns.decision: Who owns durable data, and how is application state stored and exposed?

concerns.name: Distributed state and consistency
concerns.decision: How do distributed nodes agree, partition data, order changes, and converge?

concerns.name: Data processing and analytical architecture
concerns.decision: How is data acquired, transformed, modeled, and served for analysis?

concerns.name: Reliability, availability, and recovery
concerns.decision: How does the system contain failure and restore useful service?

concerns.name: Performance, scale, and resource management
concerns.decision: How does the system meet throughput and latency goals within resource limits?

concerns.name: Deployment, runtime, and platform architecture
concerns.decision: Where do components run and how are runtime concerns composed?

concerns.name: Multitenancy and isolation
concerns.decision: How are shared platforms partitioned across tenants and failure boundaries?

concerns.name: Security, identity, and trust boundaries
concerns.decision: How is authority established, checked, delegated, and constrained?

concerns.name: Operations, observability, and control
concerns.decision: How is the system configured, monitored, governed, and kept near desired state?

concerns.name: Evolution, compatibility, and modernization
concerns.decision: How does an existing system change safely over time?

concerns.name: AI, ML, and agent systems
concerns.decision: How are learned components, retrieved knowledge, and autonomous actions composed?

concerns.name: Concurrency, specialized compute, and cyber-physical systems
concerns.decision: How are execution, timing, language processing, and physical interaction organized?

families.name: Deployment granularity
families.summary: Select the size and independence of deployable application units.

families.name: Landscape composition
families.summary: Organize autonomous capabilities across a wider application landscape.
families.observability_reason: Landscape composition spans systems and ownership beyond one repository.

families.name: Interaction topology
families.summary: Select the structural relationships between participants.

families.name: Execution organization
families.summary: Select the dominant way work and state move through the system.

families.name: Physical tiers
families.summary: Separate responsibilities across network or process boundaries.

families.name: Dependency structure
families.summary: Control dependency direction and the separation of responsibilities.

families.name: Business-logic organization
families.summary: Select where business rules and application coordination live.

families.name: Strategic domain boundaries
families.summary: Make model ownership and relationships between domains explicit.
families.observability_reason: Relationships between bounded contexts are organisational agreements; a directory or package does not prove one.

families.name: Tactical domain modeling
families.summary: Define implementation-level units that protect business invariants.

families.name: Extensibility
families.summary: Allow capabilities to vary without rebuilding the application core.

families.name: Presentation separation
families.summary: Separate state, interaction logic, and display responsibilities.

families.name: Rendering and delivery
families.summary: Choose where presentation is produced and how it becomes interactive.

families.name: Interface composition
families.summary: Assemble independently owned or server-configured user experiences.

families.name: Client state and connectivity
families.summary: Control presentation changes and behavior during interrupted connectivity.

families.name: Session placement
families.summary: Choose where conversational application state is retained.

families.name: Interface semantics
families.summary: Choose the primary interaction model exposed by a service.

families.name: Service boundary mediation
families.summary: Shape, protect, and compose calls at an application boundary.

families.name: Asynchronous conversations
families.summary: Accept work now and communicate completion separately.

families.name: Query composition
families.summary: Create a unified query experience across independently owned capabilities.

families.name: Service discovery
families.summary: Resolve logical service identities into reachable instances.

families.name: Channels and distribution
families.summary: Select the distribution and retention behavior of a messaging channel.

families.name: Message intent
families.summary: Make the meaning of an exchanged message explicit.

families.name: Routing and composition
families.summary: Control where messages go and how multiple messages are combined.

families.name: Transformation and payload
families.summary: Adapt data representations while keeping endpoints independently evolvable.

families.name: Delivery and processing safety
families.summary: Handle duplicates, publication failures, and unprocessable messages.

families.name: Correlation and ordering
families.summary: Preserve related work and make conversations identifiable.

families.name: Coordination authority
families.summary: Choose where responsibility for progress and routing resides.

families.name: Execution state
families.summary: Represent and recover multi-step work explicitly.

families.name: Cross-boundary transactions
families.summary: Coordinate changes that exceed a single local transaction boundary.

families.name: Human participation
families.summary: Make human decisions and exceptions explicit parts of execution.

families.name: Decision execution
families.summary: Separate decision definitions from general process plumbing.

families.name: Ownership boundaries
families.summary: Choose the relationship between service boundaries and persistence boundaries.

families.name: Read and write separation
families.summary: Separate authoritative updates from optimized consumption.

families.name: History and reconstruction
families.summary: Choose how historical facts relate to current application state.

families.name: Persistence mediation
families.summary: Control the boundary between domain code and storage representations.

families.name: Concurrent updates
families.summary: Detect or prevent conflicts between overlapping changes.

families.name: Replication organization
families.summary: Select which replicas may accept or coordinate updates.
families.observability_reason: Replication roles are runtime configuration of data stores, usually outside application repositories.

families.name: Agreement and authority
families.summary: Prevent conflicting decisions about shared distributed resources.
families.observability_reason: Agreement and leadership are runtime properties of a distributed system under failure.

families.name: Partitioning and placement
families.summary: Distribute state across nodes and make ownership resolvable.
families.observability_reason: Data placement across nodes is runtime and operational configuration.

families.name: Ordering and version tracking
families.summary: Represent causal or temporal relationships between distributed changes.

families.name: Replica convergence
families.summary: Repair divergence and merge changes under explicit rules.

families.name: Durable distributed logs
families.summary: Persist changes and control how replicated history is retained.

families.name: Data ingestion
families.summary: Move operational and external data into processing systems.

families.name: Analytical storage families
families.summary: Select the broad structure of an analytical data platform.

families.name: Processing topology
families.summary: Choose how batch and continuous data processing are organized.

families.name: Data organization and access
families.summary: Control responsibility, logical integration, and shared analytical access.

families.name: Analytical modeling
families.summary: Define reusable structures for analytical facts, dimensions, and historical integration.

families.name: Event analytics
families.summary: Derive results using event relationships, time, and completeness rules.

families.name: Dependency failure handling
families.summary: Bound how callers react to delayed or failed dependencies.

families.name: Failure containment
families.summary: Prevent one failure from exhausting unrelated parts of the system.

families.name: Degraded service
families.summary: Continue useful behavior when complete service is unavailable.

families.name: Availability topology
families.summary: Choose how redundant serving capacity is used.
families.observability_reason: Standby and active sites are operational topology, not repository content.

families.name: Recovery state
families.summary: Restore computation and data to an acceptable state after failure.

families.name: Cache interaction
families.summary: Choose how the cache and authoritative store interact.

families.name: Scale and workload distribution
families.summary: Spread requests and work across independently usable capacity.

families.name: Demand and admission control
families.summary: Keep demand within downstream or local processing capacity.

families.name: Work and resource efficiency
families.summary: Reduce repeated overhead and expensive contention.

families.name: Content placement
families.summary: Deliver cacheable content close to its consumers.

families.name: Runtime packaging
families.summary: Select the relationship between service instances and runtime hosts.

families.name: Runtime helpers
families.summary: Attach supporting responsibilities without embedding them in the main application.

families.name: Service networking
families.summary: Standardize connectivity and cross-service network behavior.

families.name: Placement and connectivity
families.summary: Divide deployment responsibilities across infrastructure boundaries.
families.observability_reason: Placement across on-premises, cloud and edge is an operational decision.

families.name: Release topology
families.summary: Control how a new implementation begins receiving production work.

families.name: Tenant resource models
families.summary: Select the extent to which tenant resources are dedicated or shared.
families.observability_reason: Dedicated or shared tenant resources are decided in operations and contracts.

families.name: Tenant data placement
families.summary: Choose how multiple tenants share storage structures.

families.name: Deployment and failure partitions
families.summary: Bound the number of tenants affected by a capacity or service failure.
families.observability_reason: Stamps, cells and shuffle sharding are fleet-level deployment decisions.

families.name: Tenant-aware execution
families.summary: Keep tenancy context explicit throughout requests and resource use.

families.name: Identity mediation
families.summary: Separate identity establishment from individual application implementations.

families.name: Authorization structure
families.summary: Choose where access policy is defined and enforced.

families.name: Delegation
families.summary: Pass constrained authority across system boundaries.

families.name: Containment and trust zones
families.summary: Reduce exposure and limit what a compromised component can reach.

families.name: Data and secret protection
families.summary: Reduce exposure of sensitive values and long-lived authority.

families.name: Trust posture
families.summary: Frame the assumptions under which security patterns are composed.
families.observability_reason: Trust posture is a composition of controls across a whole estate.

families.name: Operational planes
families.summary: Separate management responsibilities from the workload being managed.

families.name: Desired-state management
families.summary: Automate reconciliation of observed infrastructure and intended configuration.

families.name: Telemetry collection
families.summary: Collect and connect observations across component boundaries.

families.name: Operational and business evidence
families.summary: Retain attributable records that support investigation and reconstruction.

families.name: Health and automatic control
families.summary: Observe service condition and adjust execution using feedback.

families.name: Incremental replacement
families.summary: Replace functionality without requiring one simultaneous system cutover.
families.observability_reason: Incremental replacement is a process over time; one snapshot cannot show it.

families.name: Service extraction
families.summary: Find practical boundaries for decomposing an application.
families.observability_reason: Decomposition strategy is a design process, not a structure in the code.

families.name: Contract evolution
families.summary: Preserve interoperability while producers and consumers change.

families.name: Behavioral equivalence and migration confidence
families.summary: Compare implementations and preserve observable behavior during change.

families.name: Prediction serving
families.summary: Place model inference and feature computation in application flows.

families.name: Model lifecycle topology
families.summary: Connect model production, validation, promotion, and feedback.

families.name: Knowledge-grounded generation
families.summary: Provide relevant external knowledge to model-based generation.

families.name: LLM workflow composition
families.summary: Compose model calls with explicit task structures.

families.name: Agent coordination
families.summary: Control how tool-using agents delegate, hand off, and share responsibility.

families.name: Control and validation boundaries
families.summary: Constrain probabilistic components before their results affect authoritative state.

families.name: Concurrent execution
families.summary: Control how concurrent work is accepted, scheduled, and dispatched.

families.name: Parallel computation
families.summary: Divide computational work across processors or machines.

families.name: Real-time execution
families.summary: Organize work around explicit timing and scheduling constraints.

families.name: Physical-system control
families.summary: Connect sensing, decision-making, and actuation.

families.name: Language and execution runtimes
families.summary: Structure interpretation, compilation, and executable representations.

families.name: Edge and device integration
families.summary: Handle intermittent connectivity and local device aggregation.

entries.name: Monolithic architecture
entries.intent: Package the application as one primary deployable unit; internal structure may vary.

entries.name: Modular monolith
entries.intent: Deploy one application while enforcing explicit internal module boundaries.

entries.name: Service-based architecture
entries.intent: Divide the system into a small set of relatively coarse independently deployed services.

entries.name: Microservices architecture
entries.intent: Organize independently deployable services around cohesive capabilities with explicit contracts.

entries.name: Service-oriented architecture
entries.intent: Expose reusable business capabilities through explicit service contracts across an enterprise.

entries.name: Self-contained systems
entries.intent: Partition a landscape into autonomous applications that own their UI, logic, and data.

entries.name: Client-server
entries.intent: Assign request initiation and service provision to distinct participant roles.

entries.name: Peer-to-peer
entries.intent: Allow peers to provide and consume capabilities without a permanent central service role.

entries.name: Broker architecture
entries.intent: Use an intermediary to locate, route to, or mediate between distributed participants.

entries.name: Shared-repository architecture
entries.intent: Coordinate components through a common store of shared information.

entries.name: Blackboard architecture
entries.intent: Let specialized knowledge sources incrementally contribute to a shared problem-solving state.

entries.name: Pipes and filters
entries.intent: Compose independently implemented transformations through explicit input and output channels.

entries.name: Dataflow architecture
entries.intent: Represent computation as a graph whose operations run as their inputs become available.

entries.name: Event-driven architecture
entries.intent: Make occurrence notifications a primary way components initiate and coordinate behavior.

entries.name: Space-based architecture
entries.intent: Distribute processing and state across an in-memory space to reduce centralized database bottlenecks.

entries.name: N-tier architecture
entries.intent: Distribute application responsibilities across physical tiers; common variants are two-tier and three-tier.

entries.name: Layered architecture
entries.intent: Organize code into responsibility layers with defined dependency rules.

entries.name: Hexagonal architecture
entries.intent: Isolate application behavior behind ports implemented by external adapters.

entries.name: Onion architecture
entries.intent: Arrange dependencies inward toward the domain model through concentric responsibility boundaries.

entries.name: Clean architecture
entries.intent: Keep business policy independent of interface, delivery, and infrastructure mechanisms.

entries.name: Vertical-slice architecture
entries.intent: Organize implementation around end-to-end use cases instead of horizontal technical layers.

entries.name: Functional core, imperative shell
entries.intent: Concentrate deterministic decisions in pure functions and isolate side effects at the boundary.

entries.name: Transaction Script
entries.intent: Implement each business operation primarily as a procedure.

entries.name: Domain Model
entries.intent: Represent business concepts through collaborating objects that contain state and behavior.

entries.name: Table Module
entries.intent: Organize business logic around a table or record-set abstraction.

entries.name: Service Layer
entries.intent: Provide a stable application-operation boundary that coordinates business actions.

entries.name: Bounded Context
entries.intent: Define the boundary within which a particular domain model and vocabulary apply.

entries.name: Context Map
entries.intent: Document the relationships and translation responsibilities between bounded contexts.

entries.name: Shared Kernel
entries.intent: Share a deliberately small model subset under joint coordination between contexts.

entries.name: Customer-Supplier
entries.intent: Coordinate upstream and downstream model evolution through an explicit dependency relationship.

entries.name: Conformist
entries.intent: Have a downstream context adopt an upstream model when independent negotiation is impractical.

entries.name: Anti-Corruption Layer
entries.intent: Translate external concepts at a boundary to protect the local domain model.

entries.name: Open Host Service
entries.intent: Expose a stable integration service that multiple downstream contexts can use.

entries.name: Published Language
entries.intent: Define an explicit shared exchange language for integration between contexts.

entries.name: Partnership
entries.intent: Have dependent contexts coordinate plans and changes through a shared commitment to integration.

entries.name: Separate Ways
entries.intent: Avoid integration between contexts when the benefits do not justify the coupling and coordination costs.

entries.name: Aggregate
entries.intent: Group related domain objects behind a root that controls consistency and allowed changes.

entries.name: Entity
entries.intent: Represent a domain concept with identity that persists across changes to its attributes.

entries.name: Value Object
entries.intent: Represent a concept by its immutable descriptive value rather than independent identity.

entries.name: Domain Service
entries.intent: Place business behavior that spans concepts in an explicit domain operation.

entries.name: Specification
entries.intent: Encapsulate a composable business criterion for matching or validation.

entries.name: Domain Event
entries.intent: Represent a meaningful business occurrence within a domain model.

entries.name: Microkernel architecture
entries.intent: Keep a minimal core and provide optional behavior through extension modules.

entries.name: Plugin architecture
entries.intent: Load optional implementations through explicit extension contracts.

entries.name: Component Configurator
entries.intent: Configure or replace service components through a managed runtime configuration boundary.

entries.name: Interceptor
entries.intent: Attach cross-cutting behavior at explicitly defined interception points in a framework or invocation flow.

entries.name: Extension Interface
entries.intent: Offer separately discoverable component interfaces so capability growth does not bloat one central interface.

entries.name: Model-View-Controller
entries.intent: Assign model, presentation, and input coordination to distinct roles.

entries.name: Model-View-Presenter
entries.intent: Use a presenter to mediate between an interface abstraction and application state.

entries.name: Model-View-ViewModel
entries.intent: Expose presentation state and commands through a view model consumed by the view.

entries.name: Model-View-Intent
entries.intent: Express user intents as inputs to predictable presentation-state transitions.

entries.name: Presentation-Abstraction-Control
entries.intent: Organize interactive systems into cooperating presentation, abstraction, and control agents.

entries.name: Server-side rendering
entries.intent: Produce the initial document or interface markup on the server.

entries.name: Client-side rendering
entries.intent: Produce most interface markup and interaction state in the client.

entries.name: Static generation
entries.intent: Precompute deliverable pages or views before the user request.

entries.name: Hydration
entries.intent: Attach client interaction behavior to markup already produced elsewhere.

entries.name: Islands architecture
entries.intent: Limit client interactivity to selected independently activated page regions.

entries.name: Micro-frontends
entries.intent: Compose an interface from independently owned frontend capabilities.

entries.name: Application Shell
entries.intent: Provide persistent navigation and layout around independently loaded application content.

entries.name: Server-driven UI
entries.intent: Let a server supply constrained interface descriptions interpreted by a client renderer.

entries.name: Unidirectional data flow
entries.intent: Move user actions through a one-way state-update and rendering cycle.

entries.name: Offline-first
entries.intent: Design essential user operations to continue without a live server connection.

entries.name: Local-first
entries.intent: Treat a local replica as a primary interaction surface and synchronize shared changes afterward.

entries.name: Client Session State
entries.intent: Store session information at the client subject to integrity and privacy controls.

entries.name: Server Session State
entries.intent: Retain session information in a server-side session facility.

entries.name: Database Session State
entries.intent: Persist session information in a database shared by serving instances.

entries.name: Representational State Transfer
entries.intent: Use resource representations and a uniform interface under REST constraints.

entries.name: Remote Procedure Invocation
entries.intent: Expose remote operations through explicit invocation and return-value contracts.

entries.name: Schema-based query API
entries.intent: Let clients request shaped data through a typed query schema, as in GraphQL.

entries.name: API Gateway
entries.intent: Provide a managed entry point that routes requests to backend capabilities.

entries.name: Backends for Frontends
entries.intent: Provide backend interfaces tailored to the needs of particular client experiences.

entries.name: Remote Facade
entries.intent: Expose coarse-grained remote operations over finer-grained internal functionality.

entries.name: Gateway Routing
entries.intent: Use one boundary endpoint to select the destination service.

entries.name: Gateway Aggregation
entries.intent: Combine several backend responses into one client response at the boundary.

entries.name: Gateway Offloading
entries.intent: Move common boundary work into a shared gateway component.

entries.name: Asynchronous Request-Reply
entries.intent: Return an acknowledgement and a handle for checking or receiving a later result.

entries.name: Completion polling
entries.intent: Have the caller periodically query the state of previously accepted work.

entries.name: Callback notification
entries.intent: Notify an agreed endpoint when asynchronous work reaches a relevant state.

entries.name: Webhook subscription
entries.intent: Deliver occurrence notifications to registered remote endpoints.

entries.name: API Composition
entries.intent: Fetch and join data from the services that own it.

entries.name: Federated query API
entries.intent: Compose independently owned query schemas behind a coordinated query boundary.

entries.name: Client-side Discovery
entries.intent: Have the calling client locate and select a service instance.

entries.name: Server-side Discovery
entries.intent: Have an intermediary resolve and route requests to service instances.

entries.name: Service Registry
entries.intent: Maintain available service-instance locations and associated metadata.

entries.name: Point-to-Point Channel
entries.intent: Deliver each queued message to one eligible consumer for processing.

entries.name: Publish-Subscribe
entries.intent: Distribute a published occurrence to multiple interested subscribers.

entries.name: Message Bus
entries.intent: Provide a shared communication backbone with agreed messaging contracts.

entries.name: Replayable Event Log
entries.intent: Retain ordered event records so consumers can independently track and replay progress.

entries.name: Messaging Bridge
entries.intent: Connect messaging systems with different transports or administrative boundaries.

entries.name: Command Message
entries.intent: Ask a recipient to carry out an operation.

entries.name: Document Message
entries.intent: Transfer a meaningful data document between participants.

entries.name: Event Message
entries.intent: Announce an occurrence without directly prescribing each recipient's response.

entries.name: Content-Based Router
entries.intent: Select destinations by inspecting message content.

entries.name: Dynamic Router
entries.intent: Determine routing rules or destinations from runtime information.

entries.name: Recipient List
entries.intent: Send a message to an explicitly selected set of recipients.

entries.name: Message Filter
entries.intent: Discard messages that do not meet a consumer's criteria.

entries.name: Splitter
entries.intent: Break one composite message into independently processable messages.

entries.name: Aggregator
entries.intent: Combine related messages into a result using explicit completion rules.

entries.name: Scatter-Gather
entries.intent: Send work to multiple recipients and collect the resulting responses.

entries.name: Resequencer
entries.intent: Buffer and reorder related messages into the required processing order.

entries.name: Routing Slip
entries.intent: Carry the planned sequence of processing destinations with the message.

entries.name: Message Translator
entries.intent: Convert a message from one representation into another.

entries.name: Canonical Data Model
entries.intent: Translate integrations through an agreed exchange model to reduce pairwise mappings.

entries.name: Envelope Wrapper
entries.intent: Wrap an application payload with transport or processing metadata.

entries.name: Content Enricher
entries.intent: Add information obtained from another source to a message.

entries.name: Content Filter
entries.intent: Remove unneeded or restricted content from a message.

entries.name: Claim Check
entries.intent: Send a reference to an externally stored large payload through the messaging channel.

entries.name: Normalizer
entries.intent: Convert several incoming message forms into one processing representation.

entries.name: Idempotent Consumer
entries.intent: Ensure repeated delivery does not repeat the intended business effect.

entries.name: Transactional Outbox
entries.intent: Commit business changes and pending publication records in the same local transaction.

entries.name: Transactional Inbox
entries.intent: Record message receipt and local business changes atomically to suppress duplicate effects.

entries.name: Dead Letter Channel
entries.intent: Divert messages that cannot be delivered or processed for separate investigation.

entries.name: Retry Channel
entries.intent: Route retryable failures through a controlled delayed reprocessing path.

entries.name: Competing Consumers
entries.intent: Run multiple workers against a queue to share processing work.

entries.name: Durable Subscription
entries.intent: Retain subscriber progress or pending delivery across subscriber disconnections.

entries.name: Correlation Identifier
entries.intent: Carry an identifier that connects responses, events, or steps to the same conversation.

entries.name: Message Sequence
entries.intent: Represent an ordered multi-message logical payload with sequence metadata.

entries.name: Sequential Convoy
entries.intent: Process each related message group in order while other groups proceed independently.

entries.name: Orchestration
entries.intent: Use an explicit coordinator to direct participating activities.

entries.name: Choreography
entries.intent: Let participants react to events and coordinate without one central process controller.

entries.name: Process Manager
entries.intent: Track a conversation's state and determine which message or action comes next.

entries.name: Scheduler-Agent-Supervisor
entries.intent: Separate scheduling, execution, and progress monitoring for distributed actions.

entries.name: Durable Workflow
entries.intent: Persist workflow progress so execution can survive worker or process failures.

entries.name: State Machine
entries.intent: Express permitted execution states and transitions explicitly.

entries.name: Task Dependency Graph
entries.intent: Execute activities according to their prerequisite relationships.

entries.name: Fan-out/Fan-in
entries.intent: Launch independent activities and join them according to an explicit completion rule.

entries.name: Checkpoint and replay
entries.intent: Recover execution using persisted progress and replay under explicit determinism or reconciliation constraints.

entries.name: Saga
entries.intent: Coordinate a sequence of local transactions with recovery or compensating actions on failure.

entries.name: Compensating Transaction
entries.intent: Apply business actions that counteract prior completed work where feasible.

entries.name: Try-Confirm-Cancel
entries.intent: Reserve resources provisionally, then confirm or cancel the reservations.

entries.name: Two-Phase Commit
entries.intent: Coordinate prepare and commit decisions across participating transactional resources.

entries.name: Human Task
entries.intent: Represent assigned human work as a tracked step with inputs and completion criteria.

entries.name: Approval Gate
entries.intent: Pause a process until an authorized person supplies the required decision.

entries.name: Escalation and Timeout
entries.intent: Route overdue or unresolved work according to explicit time and ownership rules.

entries.name: Adaptive Case Management
entries.intent: Organize less predictable work around a case, its evidence, goals, and allowed actions.

entries.name: Rules Engine
entries.intent: Evaluate externalized business rules through a controlled execution component.

entries.name: Decision Table
entries.intent: Represent decisions as explicit conditions, matching rules, and resulting outputs.

entries.name: Policy as Code
entries.intent: Represent policy in machine-evaluable artifacts with versioned execution semantics.

entries.name: Shared Database
entries.intent: Allow multiple application components or services to use a shared schema or database.

entries.name: Database per Service
entries.intent: Give each service exclusive authority over its persistent data interface.

entries.name: Polyglot Persistence
entries.intent: Use different persistence models for distinct access patterns and ownership needs.

entries.name: CQRS
entries.intent: Give state-changing commands and state-reading queries distinct models or interfaces.

entries.name: Materialized View
entries.intent: Maintain a derived representation optimized for a particular query workload.

entries.name: Command-side Replica
entries.intent: Maintain a local copy of externally owned facts needed to make command decisions.

entries.name: Event-Carried State Transfer
entries.intent: Publish sufficient state in events for consumers to maintain useful local replicas.

entries.name: Event Sourcing
entries.intent: Use a persisted sequence of domain events as the authoritative history from which state is derived.

entries.name: Snapshot
entries.intent: Persist a derived state checkpoint to reduce reconstruction work.

entries.name: Temporal Data Model
entries.intent: Represent business-valid time or record-history time explicitly in the data model.

entries.name: Audit Trail
entries.intent: Retain a separate history of relevant changes and actions for inspection.

entries.name: Repository
entries.intent: Expose domain-oriented collection operations while hiding persistence details.

entries.name: Data Mapper
entries.intent: Translate between domain objects and storage records without embedding persistence in those objects.

entries.name: Active Record
entries.intent: Combine a record's domain behavior and persistence operations in the same object.

entries.name: Unit of Work
entries.intent: Track related object changes and coordinate their persistence within a transaction.

entries.name: Identity Map
entries.intent: Reuse one in-memory representation for each loaded persistent identity within a scope.

entries.name: Query Object
entries.intent: Represent a storage query through an explicit object abstraction.

entries.name: Data Gateway
entries.intent: Encapsulate access to stored rows or tables behind a dedicated access boundary.

entries.name: Optimistic Concurrency Control
entries.intent: Detect conflicting changes at commit or update time and reject or reconcile them.

entries.name: Pessimistic Concurrency Control
entries.intent: Reserve access to contested data before allowing conflicting changes.

entries.name: Multi-Version Concurrency Control
entries.intent: Maintain record versions so reads and updates can proceed under defined isolation rules.

entries.name: Leader-Follower Replication
entries.intent: Route authoritative writes through a leader and propagate them to followers.

entries.name: Multi-Leader Replication
entries.intent: Permit several leaders to accept writes and reconcile their replicated changes.

entries.name: Leaderless Replication
entries.intent: Accept requests through replicas using explicit coordination and conflict-handling rules.

entries.name: Replicated State Machine
entries.intent: Apply an agreed ordered command sequence to equivalent state machines on multiple nodes.

entries.name: Leader Election
entries.intent: Select a node authorized to coordinate a particular distributed responsibility.

entries.name: Consensus
entries.intent: Have participants agree on values or an ordered log despite specified failures.

entries.name: Quorum Coordination
entries.intent: Require intersecting response sets under defined read, write, or voting rules.

entries.name: Lease
entries.intent: Grant temporary authority that expires unless renewed.

entries.name: Fencing Token
entries.intent: Reject operations from stale owners using a monotonically advancing authority token.

entries.name: Sharding
entries.intent: Divide a logical data set into independently placed partitions.

entries.name: Hash Partitioning
entries.intent: Map keys to partitions through a hash function.

entries.name: Range Partitioning
entries.intent: Assign contiguous key ranges to partitions.

entries.name: Consistent Hashing
entries.intent: Map keys and owners so membership changes move a limited portion of keys.

entries.name: Directory-based Partitioning
entries.intent: Use a mapping service to resolve keys or partitions to their current owners.

entries.name: Lamport Clock
entries.intent: Assign logical timestamps consistent with the happened-before relation.

entries.name: Vector Clock
entries.intent: Track causal progress across participants using a vector of counters.

entries.name: Hybrid Logical Clock
entries.intent: Combine physical time with logical ordering information.

entries.name: Version Vector
entries.intent: Track per-participant update versions to detect causality and concurrent changes.

entries.name: Anti-Entropy
entries.intent: Compare replicas and exchange differences to reduce divergence.

entries.name: Read Repair
entries.intent: Detect and repair inconsistent replicas while serving reads.

entries.name: Hinted Handoff
entries.intent: Temporarily retain updates for an unavailable replica and deliver them later.

entries.name: Conflict-free Replicated Data Type
entries.intent: Use mathematically constrained data types and merge rules that support convergence.

entries.name: Write-Ahead Log
entries.intent: Record recoverable change intent before considering an update durable.

entries.name: Replicated Log
entries.intent: Copy an ordered change log to multiple nodes under defined agreement rules.

entries.name: Log Compaction
entries.intent: Reduce retained history according to state, key, or checkpoint rules without discarding required recovery information.

entries.name: ETL
entries.intent: Extract data, transform it, and then load the transformed result into the target.

entries.name: ELT
entries.intent: Load extracted data into the target platform before transforming it there.

entries.name: Change Data Capture
entries.intent: Propagate source changes rather than repeatedly copying the entire data set.

entries.name: Backfill and Replay
entries.intent: Reprocess historical input under controlled versioning and duplicate-handling rules.

entries.name: Data Warehouse
entries.intent: Organize governed integrated data for analytical consumption.

entries.name: Data Mart
entries.intent: Provide an analytical store focused on a particular business area or audience.

entries.name: Data Lake
entries.intent: Retain diverse raw or lightly processed data for later interpretation and processing.

entries.name: Lakehouse
entries.intent: Combine lake-style storage with managed table, transaction, and analytical-serving capabilities.

entries.name: Batch Processing
entries.intent: Process bounded data sets as scheduled or triggered jobs.

entries.name: Stream Processing
entries.intent: Continuously process incoming records and maintain running state or results.

entries.name: Micro-batch Processing
entries.intent: Process a continuing input stream as successive small bounded batches.

entries.name: Lambda Architecture
entries.intent: Combine separate batch and speed paths with a serving layer.

entries.name: Kappa Architecture
entries.intent: Center processing on a replayable stream rather than separate batch and speed implementations.

entries.name: Hub-and-Spoke Data Warehouse
entries.intent: Use an integrated warehouse hub to supply dependent analytical data marts.

entries.name: Data Mesh
entries.intent: Distribute data-product ownership by domain with shared platform and federated governance principles.

entries.name: Data Virtualization
entries.intent: Expose a logical data-access layer over separately stored sources.

entries.name: Federated Query
entries.intent: Execute coordinated queries across multiple data stores without requiring one physical store.

entries.name: Medallion Data Layers
entries.intent: Progressively refine data through quality and serving layers; common names are bronze, silver, and gold.

entries.name: Star Schema
entries.intent: Organize fact tables around directly connected dimension tables.

entries.name: Snowflake Schema
entries.intent: Normalize some dimension structures into related dimension tables.

entries.name: Data Vault
entries.intent: Organize historical integration around hubs, links, and descriptive satellites.

entries.name: Anchor Modeling
entries.intent: Use highly decomposed structures to support evolving attributes and historical modeling.

entries.name: Windowed Aggregation
entries.intent: Aggregate events within explicitly defined count, key, or time windows.

entries.name: Event Time and Watermarks
entries.intent: Process according to event occurrence time with an explicit estimate of progress and lateness.

entries.name: Complex Event Processing
entries.intent: Recognize meaningful event combinations, temporal relationships, or sequences.

entries.name: Retry
entries.intent: Repeat an operation only for failures and conditions judged retryable.

entries.name: Exponential Backoff with Jitter
entries.intent: Spread retries in time to avoid synchronized overload.

entries.name: Timeout and Deadline Propagation
entries.intent: Bound waiting and carry an end-to-end time budget across dependency calls.

entries.name: Circuit Breaker
entries.intent: Stop repeated calls to a failing dependency and probe for recovery.

entries.name: Bulkhead
entries.intent: Separate resources or execution pools so one failing workload cannot consume all capacity.

entries.name: Fail Fast
entries.intent: Reject work promptly when its required preconditions or dependencies cannot be satisfied.

entries.name: Supervision Tree
entries.intent: Have supervisors monitor child processes and apply explicit restart or escalation policies.

entries.name: Fallback
entries.intent: Use an explicitly defined alternative when the preferred operation cannot succeed.

entries.name: Graceful Degradation
entries.intent: Reduce optional capabilities while preserving the most valuable supported behavior.

entries.name: Static Response
entries.intent: Return a predefined safe response when dynamic processing is unavailable or unnecessary.

entries.name: Active-Passive
entries.intent: Keep a standby instance or site ready to take over from the active one.

entries.name: Active-Active
entries.intent: Serve work from multiple active instances or sites under explicit state and routing rules.

entries.name: Warm Standby
entries.intent: Maintain a smaller functioning recovery environment that can be expanded.

entries.name: Pilot Light
entries.intent: Keep essential recovery foundations available while bringing remaining resources online after a failure.

entries.name: Checkpoint-Restart
entries.intent: Resume computation from a durable state checkpoint.

entries.name: Backup and Restore
entries.intent: Recover data and configuration from retained recovery copies.

entries.name: Point-in-Time Recovery
entries.intent: Reconstruct stored data to a selected recoverable time using backups and change history.

entries.name: Health-Based Failover
entries.intent: Switch traffic or responsibility when explicit health criteria indicate a failure.

entries.name: Cache-Aside
entries.intent: Have application code populate cached values on misses and manage invalidation.

entries.name: Read-Through Cache
entries.intent: Let the caching layer load missing values from the authoritative store.

entries.name: Write-Through Cache
entries.intent: Write through the cache boundary to the backing store before reporting completion.

entries.name: Write-Behind Cache
entries.intent: Buffer updates in the cache layer and persist them asynchronously with explicit durability semantics.

entries.name: Refresh-Ahead
entries.intent: Refresh likely-to-be-needed values before their cached versions expire.

entries.name: Stale-While-Revalidate
entries.intent: Serve an allowed stale value while refreshing the value asynchronously.

entries.name: Load-Balanced Stateless Replicas
entries.intent: Distribute requests across interchangeable serving instances with state externalized as needed.

entries.name: Partitioned Workers
entries.intent: Assign independent key or work partitions to workers with explicit ownership.

entries.name: Queue-Based Load Leveling
entries.intent: Buffer incoming work to smooth bursts before backend processing.

entries.name: Priority Queue
entries.intent: Choose work order using explicit priority and fairness rules.

entries.name: Backpressure
entries.intent: Signal limited capacity upstream so producers reduce or pause work.

entries.name: Rate Limiting
entries.intent: Bound allowed activity over a defined interval or token budget.

entries.name: Throttling
entries.intent: Constrain consumption or acceptance of work to protect service limits.

entries.name: Load Shedding
entries.intent: Reject or discard selected work when accepting it would damage overall service.

entries.name: Admission Control
entries.intent: Decide whether to admit work based on available capacity and resource requirements.

entries.name: Batching
entries.intent: Combine several operations into one processing or transport unit.

entries.name: Pipelining
entries.intent: Overlap operations so several stages or requests progress concurrently.

entries.name: Request Coalescing
entries.intent: Combine equivalent concurrent requests into one underlying operation.

entries.name: Connection Pool
entries.intent: Reuse bounded connections instead of repeatedly creating them.

entries.name: Object Pool
entries.intent: Reuse costly objects under controlled ownership and capacity limits.

entries.name: Static Content Hosting
entries.intent: Serve immutable or static assets from a dedicated content-delivery surface.

entries.name: Edge Caching
entries.intent: Place eligible cached content near users with explicit freshness and invalidation rules.

entries.name: Content Delivery Network
entries.intent: Use a distributed delivery network to serve content from geographically suitable locations.

entries.name: Service Instance per Host
entries.intent: Give each service instance its own host-level runtime boundary.

entries.name: Service Instance per Container
entries.intent: Package a service instance in an isolated container runtime unit.

entries.name: Serverless Execution
entries.intent: Delegate provisioning and scaling of execution capacity to a managed runtime.

entries.name: Immutable Deployment
entries.intent: Replace deployed instances with newly built artifacts instead of changing instances in place.

entries.name: Sidecar
entries.intent: Deploy a supporting component alongside an application with an intentionally coupled lifecycle.

entries.name: Ambassador
entries.intent: Use a helper to handle outgoing communication on behalf of the application.

entries.name: Adapter Container
entries.intent: Use a co-located helper to normalize an application's interface or output.

entries.name: Service Mesh
entries.intent: Apply shared service-to-service network behavior through an infrastructure layer.

entries.name: Node-Level Proxy
entries.intent: Share network mediation across workloads on a node rather than attaching one proxy to every workload.

entries.name: Hub-and-Spoke Network
entries.intent: Connect workload networks through a controlled shared connectivity hub.

entries.name: Hybrid Split Deployment
entries.intent: Place selected application or data responsibilities on different on-premises and cloud environments.

entries.name: Cloud Bursting
entries.intent: Expand selected workload execution into additional cloud capacity when local capacity is insufficient.

entries.name: Edge-Cloud Split
entries.intent: Place time-sensitive or local work at the edge and coordinated processing in central infrastructure.

entries.name: Disconnected Deployment
entries.intent: Operate within an isolated environment using explicit transfer, update, and synchronization boundaries.

entries.name: Blue-Green Deployment
entries.intent: Maintain two environments and switch serving traffic to the newly validated version.

entries.name: Canary Deployment
entries.intent: Expose a new version to a limited population before expanding its traffic.

entries.name: Rolling Deployment
entries.intent: Replace serving instances incrementally while the service remains available.

entries.name: Shadow Deployment
entries.intent: Send copied inputs to a non-authoritative implementation while controlling its side effects.

entries.name: Silo Model
entries.intent: Give a tenant dedicated resources for the selected isolation boundary.

entries.name: Pool Model
entries.intent: Share resources between tenants with explicit logical isolation.

entries.name: Bridge Model
entries.intent: Combine silo and pool approaches across layers or tenant groups.

entries.name: Database per Tenant
entries.intent: Place each tenant's selected data in a dedicated database.

entries.name: Schema per Tenant
entries.intent: Separate tenant data into distinct schemas within a shared database system.

entries.name: Shared Tables with Tenant Keys
entries.intent: Co-locate tenant rows while enforcing tenant identity in access and query paths.

entries.name: Deployment Stamp
entries.intent: Repeat a complete application deployment unit and assign tenants or workloads to instances.

entries.name: Cell-Based Architecture
entries.intent: Place workloads in independently bounded cells to contain failures and limit blast radius.

entries.name: Shuffle Sharding
entries.intent: Assign overlapping subsets of resources so unrelated customers rarely share an entire failure set.

entries.name: Tenant Context Propagation
entries.intent: Carry verified tenant identity through all relevant execution and data-access boundaries.

entries.name: Per-Tenant Quotas
entries.intent: Apply tenant-specific resource budgets or limits.

entries.name: Tenant-Aware Routing
entries.intent: Route work according to tenant placement, isolation, or service-tier rules.

entries.name: Identity Federation
entries.intent: Accept identities through a defined trust relationship with external identity providers.

entries.name: Identity Broker
entries.intent: Mediate identity exchange between applications and one or more identity providers.

entries.name: Workload Identity
entries.intent: Give running software verifiable identities for service-to-service access.

entries.name: Policy Decision and Enforcement Separation
entries.intent: Separate policy evaluation from the components that enforce access decisions.

entries.name: Reference Monitor
entries.intent: Mediate protected resource access through an explicitly trusted enforcement component.

entries.name: Role-Based Access Control
entries.intent: Express permissions through assigned roles.

entries.name: Attribute-Based Access Control
entries.intent: Evaluate access using attributes of subjects, resources, actions, and context.

entries.name: Relationship-Based Access Control
entries.intent: Evaluate access using relevant relationships between subjects and resources.

entries.name: Token Exchange
entries.intent: Convert an accepted security token into one suitable for a downstream audience and delegation scope.

entries.name: Valet Key
entries.intent: Grant narrow direct access to a resource using a constrained temporary credential.

entries.name: Capability-Based Security
entries.intent: Represent authority through possession of explicit unforgeable capabilities.

entries.name: Security Reverse Proxy
entries.intent: Enforce selected security checks at a controlled inbound service boundary.

entries.name: Bastion
entries.intent: Provide a deliberately restricted administrative entry point.

entries.name: Microsegmentation
entries.intent: Constrain lateral communication using fine-grained network or workload boundaries.

entries.name: Sandbox
entries.intent: Run less-trusted code or content with restricted resources and authority.

entries.name: Envelope Encryption
entries.intent: Encrypt data with data keys that are protected by separate wrapping keys.

entries.name: Tokenization
entries.intent: Replace sensitive values with references resolved through a protected token service.

entries.name: Secret Broker
entries.intent: Provide controlled retrieval or issuance of secrets without embedding them in application artifacts.

entries.name: Zero Trust
entries.intent: Continuously evaluate access under explicit identity, context, and least-privilege assumptions.

entries.name: Defense in Depth
entries.intent: Compose independent protective controls across relevant failure and attack paths.

entries.name: Control Plane and Data Plane Separation
entries.intent: Separate configuration and orchestration decisions from request or data processing.

entries.name: Management Plane
entries.intent: Provide a bounded administrative surface for operational lifecycle actions.

entries.name: Reconciliation Loop
entries.intent: Repeatedly compare observed state with desired state and apply bounded corrective actions.

entries.name: Operator
entries.intent: Encode application-specific lifecycle knowledge in controllers acting on declared resources.

entries.name: External Configuration Store
entries.intent: Keep operational configuration outside application deployment packages.

entries.name: Microservice Chassis
entries.intent: Provide reusable infrastructure support for recurring service-level operational concerns.

entries.name: Telemetry Agent
entries.intent: Collect observations near a workload and forward them to processing infrastructure.

entries.name: Telemetry Gateway
entries.intent: Centralize telemetry processing and export for a group of workloads.

entries.name: Centralized Log Aggregation
entries.intent: Collect distributed component logs into a shared searchable system.

entries.name: Distributed Trace Context Propagation
entries.intent: Carry request and span relationships across asynchronous and synchronous boundaries.

entries.name: Append-Only Audit Ledger
entries.intent: Record significant operational or business actions without ordinary in-place history rewriting.

entries.name: Tamper-Evident Logging
entries.intent: Make unauthorized alteration of retained records detectable under explicit trust assumptions.

entries.name: Provenance Capture
entries.intent: Record the origins, transformations, and responsible actors associated with results or artifacts.

entries.name: Health Endpoint Monitoring
entries.intent: Expose explicit health observations for external monitoring or routing decisions.

entries.name: Watchdog
entries.intent: Monitor a process or control loop and trigger a defined recovery action if it stops progressing.

entries.name: Autoscaling Feedback Loop
entries.intent: Adjust serving capacity using measurements, policies, delays, and stabilization rules.

entries.name: Strangler Fig
entries.intent: Gradually redirect capabilities from an existing system into replacement implementations.

entries.name: Branch by Abstraction
entries.intent: Introduce a stable abstraction so implementations can be replaced incrementally.

entries.name: Parallel Run
entries.intent: Operate old and new implementations together and compare results before transferring authority.

entries.name: Expand-Contract
entries.intent: Introduce compatible additions, migrate consumers, and only then remove the old interface or representation.

entries.name: Decompose by Business Capability
entries.intent: Align extracted units with cohesive business capabilities.

entries.name: Decompose by Subdomain
entries.intent: Use domain analysis to identify candidate boundaries for separately evolving capabilities.

entries.name: Decompose by Transaction Boundary
entries.intent: Keep strongly coupled changes together where local atomicity is a dominant requirement.

entries.name: Versioned Contract
entries.intent: Identify supported API, event, or schema contract versions explicitly.

entries.name: Tolerant Reader
entries.intent: Consume only required fields while handling compatible additions according to defined validation rules.

entries.name: Schema Registry
entries.intent: Manage schema identity, versions, and compatibility rules in a shared contract facility.

entries.name: Consumer-Driven Contract Testing
entries.intent: Verify provider behavior against explicit expectations supplied by its consumers.

entries.name: Characterization Testing
entries.intent: Capture existing observable behavior before changing the implementation.

entries.name: Differential Testing
entries.intent: Run equivalent cases against implementations and inspect meaningful output differences.

entries.name: Recorded Traffic Replay
entries.intent: Exercise a replacement with recorded interactions under controlled data and side-effect rules.

entries.name: Reconciliation
entries.intent: Compare authoritative and migrated states and resolve discrepancies before or after cutover.

entries.name: Batch Inference
entries.intent: Generate predictions for bounded sets of records in scheduled or triggered jobs.

entries.name: Online Inference
entries.intent: Serve model predictions within an interactive request path.

entries.name: Streaming Inference
entries.intent: Apply inference continuously to an incoming event stream.

entries.name: Two-Stage Retrieval and Ranking
entries.intent: Retrieve candidates cheaply and rank the smaller set with a more expensive model.

entries.name: Online-Offline Feature Store
entries.intent: Coordinate reusable features across training and low-latency serving paths.

entries.name: Training Pipeline
entries.intent: Represent repeatable data preparation, training, and validation as explicit pipeline stages.

entries.name: Registry-Mediated Model Promotion
entries.intent: Promote versioned model artifacts through a controlled registry and deployment boundary.

entries.name: Feedback-Driven Retraining
entries.intent: Use monitored outcomes and approved triggers to initiate a new training and validation cycle.

entries.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entries.intent: Retrieve task-relevant material and supply it as grounding context to a generative model.

entries.name: Hybrid Retrieval
entries.intent: Combine lexical and semantic retrieval signals under an explicit result-merging strategy.

entries.name: Retrieve-Then-Rerank
entries.intent: Use a second scoring stage to refine an initially retrieved candidate set.

entries.name: GraphRAG
entries.intent: Use graph-derived structure or summaries in retrieval and grounding; implementations vary substantially.

entries.name: Agentic Retrieval
entries.intent: Let a model iteratively choose retrieval steps under bounded execution and access rules.

entries.name: Prompt Chaining
entries.intent: Pass results through predefined stages of model-based transformation.

entries.name: Model Routing
entries.intent: Select a model or specialized processing path according to the task.

entries.name: Parallel Model Calls
entries.intent: Run independent model operations and combine their results using explicit aggregation rules.

entries.name: Orchestrator-Workers
entries.intent: Have an orchestrator decompose work and delegate specialized activities.

entries.name: Evaluator-Optimizer
entries.intent: Iterate between producing a candidate and evaluating it against defined criteria.

entries.name: Single Agent with Tools
entries.intent: Let one bounded agent select and invoke tools to pursue a task.

entries.name: Supervisor-Worker Agents
entries.intent: Use a supervising agent to assign and coordinate specialized agent work.

entries.name: Agent Handoff
entries.intent: Transfer control and selected context to a different specialized agent.

entries.name: Shared-Conversation Agents
entries.intent: Coordinate multiple agents through a managed conversation with explicit turn and termination rules.

entries.name: Model Gateway
entries.intent: Mediate model access through shared routing, identity, budget, and observation controls.

entries.name: Model Cascade
entries.intent: Escalate from cheaper or narrower models to more capable models under explicit acceptance rules.

entries.name: Structured Output Validation
entries.intent: Check generated outputs against schemas and business constraints before downstream use.

entries.name: Deterministic Execution Around Model Decisions
entries.intent: Keep authorization, state changes, and execution guarantees in explicit code around learned decisions.

entries.name: Retrieval-Backed Agent Memory
entries.intent: Persist selected task experience externally and retrieve it under bounded relevance and access rules.

entries.name: Actor Model
entries.intent: Represent stateful participants as independently addressed message-processing actors.

entries.name: Active Object
entries.intent: Separate a method's invocation from its execution using an explicit scheduling boundary.

entries.name: Reactor
entries.intent: Dispatch handlers when synchronous event demultiplexing reports readiness.

entries.name: Proactor
entries.intent: Dispatch completion handlers for operations performed asynchronously.

entries.name: Half-Sync/Half-Async
entries.intent: Separate synchronous application work from asynchronous lower-level processing.

entries.name: Leader/Followers Thread Pool
entries.intent: Rotate thread leadership for waiting on and dispatching events.

entries.name: Monitor Object
entries.intent: Serialize access to an object's state using controlled synchronization and condition coordination.

entries.name: Acceptor-Connector
entries.intent: Separate connection establishment and service initialization from subsequent connection processing.

entries.name: Master-Worker
entries.intent: Have a coordinator distribute work among independently executing workers.

entries.name: Fork-Join
entries.intent: Split a computation into parallel subcomputations and combine their results.

entries.name: MapReduce
entries.intent: Transform partitions into intermediate keyed results and combine values by key.

entries.name: Bulk Synchronous Parallel
entries.intent: Organize parallel computation into local work, communication, and synchronization phases.

entries.name: Data Parallelism
entries.intent: Apply equivalent computations to different partitions of input data.

entries.name: Pipeline Parallelism
entries.intent: Execute different computational stages concurrently across work items.

entries.name: Model Parallelism
entries.intent: Partition a model's computations across execution resources.

entries.name: Cyclic Executive
entries.intent: Execute scheduled tasks according to a repeating predetermined cycle.

entries.name: Time-Triggered Architecture
entries.intent: Initiate coordinated actions according to an explicit time schedule.

entries.name: Event-Triggered Architecture
entries.intent: Initiate processing in response to external or internal events.

entries.name: Interrupt-to-Task Deferral
entries.intent: Keep immediate interrupt handling bounded and defer longer processing to scheduled tasks.

entries.name: Feedback Control Loop
entries.intent: Adjust actions using observed differences between measured and desired conditions.

entries.name: Hierarchical Control
entries.intent: Arrange controllers at levels with distinct time horizons and responsibilities.

entries.name: Sense-Plan-Act
entries.intent: Separate environment observation, action planning, and action execution.

entries.name: Subsumption Architecture
entries.intent: Layer reactive behaviors so higher-level behavior can suppress or influence lower-level behavior.

entries.name: Digital Twin
entries.intent: Maintain a software representation of a physical system connected to its observations and state.

entries.name: Compiler Pipeline
entries.intent: Transform source through explicit analysis and generation stages.

entries.name: Interpreter Architecture
entries.intent: Execute program meaning through an interpreter operating on a program representation.

entries.name: Virtual Machine
entries.intent: Execute an abstract instruction set through a portable or isolated runtime.

entries.name: Intermediate Representation
entries.intent: Use a defined internal program representation between analysis and generation stages.

entries.name: Just-in-Time Compilation
entries.intent: Compile selected program portions during execution.

entries.name: Tiered Compilation
entries.intent: Move execution between interpretation or compiled tiers based on runtime information.

entries.name: Store-and-Forward
entries.intent: Persist outgoing data locally and transmit it when connectivity becomes available.

entries.name: Device Gateway
entries.intent: Mediate device protocols, identities, aggregation, and upstream communication at an edge boundary.

antipatterns.name: Distributed monolith
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Coordinated deployments, shared release coupling, chatty calls, or hidden shared data dependencies

antipatterns.name: Big ball of mud
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Unclear ownership and uncontrolled dependencies across responsibilities

antipatterns.name: God service or god module
antipatterns.typical_evidence: One unit owns unrelated behavior and becomes a change bottleneck

antipatterns.name: Uncontrolled shared database
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Services bypass ownership boundaries and depend directly on each other's storage details

antipatterns.name: Chatty synchronous service chain
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Many serial remote calls amplify latency and failure

antipatterns.name: Dual-write gap
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Database updates and message publication can succeed independently

antipatterns.name: Retry storm
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Many callers repeatedly retry the same overloaded dependency

antipatterns.name: Unbounded concurrency
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Accepted work grows without resource limits or backpressure

antipatterns.name: Uncontrolled agent loop
antipatterns.typical_evidence: Repeated model or tool calls without progress or bounded authority
